2023_063_elementary_mathematics_material.paragraph: Elementary Mathematics Materials Adoption recommendation dated March 2023 and submitted by Natalie Haezebrouck and Julia Alder, proposing that Troy School District adopt Bridges in Mathematics and Number Corner, 3rd edition, from The Math Learning Center for grades K-5. The district's last elementary math adoption was in 2010, and 95 early adopter teachers across eleven elementary buildings volunteered to implement Bridges and Number Corner during the 2022-23 school year. The Math Learning Center sales order quote Q-10092 carries a subtotal of $425,233.00 and a net total of $443,974.31 including shipping, and the summary of cost puts the projected total for the adoption at $535,592.31.
2023_063_elementary_mathematics_material.page:
**Submission**
Elementary Mathematics Materials Adoption, March 2023, submitted by Natalie Haezebrouck and Julia Alder.

**Rationale**
Troy School District reviews curricular materials every nine years. The last curricular adoption was Middle and High-School Health in 2020; the last elementary math adoption was in 2010. The philosophy of review has since broadened from seeking new materials to examining instructional practices, intervention, assessment and current data so that curricular, structural and staffing needs align. Teachers have been supplementing the current resource with three act tasks, number sense routines and additional materials; a resource addressing deep conceptual learning, number sense and mathematical fluency is sought. Reference points are the Michigan Math State Standards and the National Council of Teachers of Mathematics (NCTM).

**Process**
The Math Leadership Team (MLT) was assembled in September 2019 with representation from all grade levels and roles. MLT reviewed student performance data, surveyed all elementary teachers, and studied NCTM's Principles to Action, concluding that both a math specialist role and new curricular materials were needed. MLT members and colleagues from the Oakland County Math Leadership Team identified candidate publishers and materials, evaluated against the Standards for Mathematical Practice and NCTM's 8 Effective Math Teaching Practices. Early Adopter teachers spent over a year evaluating materials. In January 2021 the list was narrowed and select publishers were invited to Troy to demonstrate online features; materials were piloted in January and February. Ninety-five early adopter teachers volunteered to implement Bridges in Mathematics and Number Corner during 2022-23.

**Early Adopter Team by building**

| Building | Total |
|---|---|
| Barnard | 6 |
| Bemis | 6 |
| Costello | 9 |
| Hamilton | 18 |
| Hill | 6 |
| Leonard | 17 |
| Martell | 12 |
| Morse | 6 |
| Troy Union | 9 |
| Wass | 4 |
| Wattles | 2 |
| Total | 95 |

Grade-level totals are 13 in K, 22 in grade 1, 13 in grade 2, 15 in grade 3, 16 in grade 4 and 16 in grade 5.

**Materials reviewed**
Illustrative Mathematics (not fully available during the 2021-2022 pilot window, Google Drive format, now more available from Kendall Hunt); Math Expressions 2013 Edition, the current resource; and Bridges Mathematics including Number Corner. Number Corner is described as a skill-building program built around the classroom calendar providing 15-20 minutes of additional daily instruction.

**Recommendation and implementation**
Bridges Math and Number Corner 3rd edition are recommended. All resources are to be available on the first day of school for 2023-24, with optional June training on Number Corner and Bridges Unit 1, a district-wide kick-off during back-to-school professional development in August 2023 tied to the OneTroy kick-off, job-embedded PD, math specialist support in each building, and master schedules built to incorporate 75-90 minutes of math instructional time per day.

**Summary of cost**

|---|---|
| Bridges Mathematics Second Edition | $443,974.31 |
| Updated Number Corner Third Edition Update Package | $48,000.00 |
| Additional Manipulatives & Number Corner Poster Printing | $32,368.47 |
| For organizing workplaces and additional classroom manipulatives | $11,250 |
| Total Cost | $535,592.31 |
2023_063_elementary_mathematics_material.verbose:
Elementary Mathematics Materials Adoption report, March 2023, submitted by Natalie Haezebrouck and Julia Alder to the Troy School District Board of Education.

RATIONALE. The district reviews its curricular materials every nine years. Since the last curricular adoption, Middle and High-School Health in 2020, the district has updated its philosophy of curricular review: rather than simply seeking new materials, it takes stock of programming as a whole, including instructional practices, intervention, assessment and current data, so that curricular, structural and staffing needs can be aligned. The last elementary math adoption was conducted in 2010. Since then the district reports better understanding of the Michigan Math State Standards, better aligned elementary math resources, and continued guidance from the National Council of Teachers of Mathematics (NCTM) on best practice. Teachers have been supplementing the current resource with three act tasks, number sense routines and additional materials to address missed opportunities, and a resource that fully addresses deep conceptual learning, number sense and mathematical fluency is desired.

PROGRAM REVIEW TIMELINE (Image 1). The timeline traces comprehensive math program development and the development of MTSS: learning and implementing Math Recovery and Tier 1 research in research classrooms; 2019 Bridges early adopters with Tier 1 focus on conceptual understanding and modeling; '20 COVID, extension of ME and math specialists, support for intensive intervention in math and research of resources for Tier 1; '21 review of TSD data and focus on math mindset, noting a trend of fewer students proficient in math over time; and 22-23.

PROCESS AND SELECTION. The review began in September 2019 with the assembly of the Math Leadership Team (MLT), an interdepartmental team with representation from all grade levels and roles across the system that meets several times per year to plan and monitor progress toward the district vision. MLT reviewed student performance data and administered a survey to all elementary teachers about their own and their students' experience with mathematics, and studied the NCTM publication Principles to Action. Through that work the team identified a need for the role of math specialist as well as a need for new curricular materials. Members of MLT and colleagues from the Oakland County Math Leadership Team identified potential publishers, materials and resources, using the standards of math practice (Table 2) and the NCTM Effective Math Teaching Practices to focus the evaluation, with the Michigan Standards for Mathematics as the foundation. Image 2 presents the 8 Effective Math Teaching Practices, cited to NCTM (2014), Principals to Actions: Ensuring mathematical success for all. Once selections were narrowed, the Early Adopter Team vetted the resources and began using lessons in classrooms; all early adopter teachers spent over a year evaluating materials. In January 2021 the resource list was narrowed and select publishers were invited to Troy to demonstrate online features accompanying the text resources; materials were piloted in January and February. Ninety-five early adopter teachers volunteered to implement the recommended curriculum, Bridges in Mathematics and Number Corner, during the 2022-23 school year.

MATERIALS REVIEWED (Table 3). Illustrative Mathematics develops conceptual understanding with tasks that call for hands-on learning, but was not fully available during the 2021-2022 pilot and review timeline; its format was in Google Drive, publishers are not developing more supports for elementary level IM, hands-on materials and mathematical modeling tools are not integrated within the resource, and online Google Drive modules for teachers require multiple downloads and integration to Schoology. It is now more available from Kendall Hunt and through online modules, and is quoted as rigorous, problem-based, fully aligned to the standards, available in print and digital, and highly rated by EdReports across all three review gateways. Math Expressions 2013 Edition is the current resource; its approach to mathematical fluency was limited and only partially addressed number sense, it aligned with grade-level content but did not adequately address differentiation, ELD and students with special needs, its online personal math trainer provided extra practice, hands-on materials and modeling tools are not integrated, and online teacher resources are available but difficult to utilize. Bridges Mathematics including Number Corner offers a fluency approach embedded in Number Corner with monthly opportunities for students to share, model and develop numeracy; it aligns with grade-level content and integrates research and models supporting Math Recovery learning progressions; tasks build in varying levels of sophistication; modeling tools provide access for differentiation including ELD, students with special needs, and students with high sophistication in math; teacher website and materials are available in PDF; online apps and family supports come through the Math Learning Center website; an active online support blog draws on a national network of educators; and a Fluency Pathway sits in Number Corner. Number Corner is described as a skill-building program revolving around the classroom calendar that provides daily practice and continual encounters with broader mathematical concepts in 15-20 minutes of additional engaging daily instruction.

FEATURES OF RECOMMENDED MATERIALS (Table 4). Features include a number sense focus through Number Corner; grade-level alignment through Bridges units addressing the Michigan State Standards; teacher implementation supports through the Math Learning Center Educator Website, which requires an educator login and which math specialists use to find recommendations and resources for early adopter classroom teachers; parent communication through Math At Home and Home Learning Resources; digital features through Math Learning Center iPad apps and Work Place games with sharable QR codes; fluency and practice through Home Connections and student workbooks, with the district holding an option to print or purchase workbooks; an assessment system with pre-assessments, check points, post-assessments, checklists, and both interview-based and written forms; support for high aptitude, ELD, special needs and DEI through low-floor high-ceiling task design with built-in mathematical tools and models; and implementation support including multiple professional learning sessions included in the purchase, partnership with a local facilitator for job-embedded learning, and the Bridges educator blog. The recommendation is that Bridges Math and Number Corner 3rd edition move forward.

IMPLEMENTATION PLAN. All resources will be available for instruction on the first day of school for the 2023-24 academic year. Teachers will have the option of training on Number Corner and Bridges Unit 1 in June, and all teachers will participate in a kick-off during back-to-school professional development in August 2023 in collaboration with math specialists and the Bridges team during the OneTroy kick-off. Teachers will participate in job-embedded PD, math specialists will support each building throughout the year, and the district will work with principals to create master schedules incorporating 75-90 minutes of instructional time per day.
